short: HuBERT-unit, pitch and energy targets (M02) and flow post-net (M06) are standard, after ReVISE and VCVTS; GRID WER 17.07% vs 17.62%; seen-speaker tests only (M12 behind).
position: The paper [@kim2024let] changes the training targets (M02: 200 HuBERT units, pitch and energy from the paired audio) and the decoder (M06: variance predictors and a flow post-net); both are standard, the units follow ReVISE [@hsu2023revise] and the unit-plus-pitch design VCVTS [@wang2022vcvts], neither cited, and the ablations do not single out the units. The "large margin" holds for MOS and for Lip2Wav WER (34.71% against 48.73% for VCA-GAN), but GRID WER is 17.07% against 17.62% under a scorer at 12.20% on real speech (Table 1). Its test sets draw on the training speakers (Sec. Datasets), behind earlier unseen-speaker GRID tests including its own comparator [@kim2021vcagan]. On LRS3, which the paper did not use, two [later] re-runs by the authors' group give 79.7% and 84.08% WER under different scorers, against 28.5% and 30.45% for their successors [@choi2024v2sflow; @kim2025faces].
